text:
maria: Heads-up — saw a weird pattern on prod yesterday: lots of tiny 100-200 token requests from a handful of keys that spiked for ~10s and blasted past their steady allowance. Other orgs got queued. Thinking we need a short-burst budget separate from steady-state token buckets.

kevin: Saw that too. Was the burst coming from one IP range or multiple keys?

maria: Multiple keys, same org. Traffic cone: ~5 keys did ~50 reqs each in 7s window. Not sustained but enough to saturate our per-GPU concurrency.

ashok: Proposal: two-layer enforcement. Keep current token-bucket for long-term rate, add a small high-frequency windowed budget (e.g., 1s/10s) that caps short spikes. If the short budget is exhausted, apply soft-backpressure (429 with Retry-After) instead of hard drop.

erin: Agree on layered approach. UX question: do we expose short-burst slots in Console (per-org) or keep it internal tuning only?

kevin: We should surface it but not as editable by default. Maybe 'Burst budget: auto / custom'. Default auto picks based on historical qps variance and customer tier.

maria: Auto tuning sounds right. We can expose an override for enterprise accounts. For defaults, measurement needs: peak-per-minute / peak-per-10s / cv of inter-arrival.

ashok: Example config snippet I sketched:
```yaml
burst_policy:
  short_window_ms: 10000 # 10s
  short_tokens: 200
  short_refill_per_s: 20
  steady_window_s: 60
  steady_tokens: 1000
  refill_rate_steady_per_s: 16.6
  short_failsafe: retry_after 1s
```

kevin: Two quick questions: 1) should short_tokens be per-key or per-org? 2) how do we prevent key churn to escape short budgets?

erin: I vote per-key + per-org aggregate. Per-key prevents one key from stomping others, per-org aggregate prevents many keys spinning up to game the system.

simon: Sounds good. Implementation detail: token buckets in our proxy are O(1) per-request, but maintaining both per-key and per-org state doubles memory. We can use TTL for short buckets (expire after 30s idle) to limit memory.

maria: Also consider per-route weights — embeddings vs generation. Embeddings are cheap but often batched; generation is expensive. Short budget should be scaled by route type.

ashok: Agreed. For testing, I want an e2e sim comparing: (A) token-bucket-only, (B) two-layer with soft 429, (C) two-layer with immediate queueing. Metrics: p95 latency for normal orgs, error rate, tail latency for spiked org, cost (GPU-seconds wasted).

kevin: Can we add a circuit-breaker metric to the dashboard? e.g., "short_burst_blocked" count and per-org time series plus top offending keys. Ops wants to alert when >X blocked/s.

maria: Yes — dashboard mock: small panel per-org: short_burst_used_vs_alloc, short_burst_blocked_rate, steady_bucket_util. Add annotation when canary rollouts changed policy.

ops-bot: Incident summary created: INC-2027-0442 - short-burst saturation. Link: https://incidents.local/INC-2027-0442

erin: Regarding client backpressure: do we prefer Retry-After header vs custom error body with suggested backoff? Many clients ignore Retry-After.

kevin: We should do both. 429 + Retry-After + light JSON: {"code":"burst_limit","recommended_backoff_s":1}. Also emit a trace/span tag so we can correlate on the Console traces view.

maria: For rollout: default on for 10% of traffic in staging then 100% in prod with feature flag. Canary target should be high-variance orgs first.

ashok: I'll prototype in the proxy repo. Plan: implement short-burst bucket TTL, per-key + per-org aggregate check, soft-429 path, metric emissions. Need an API review for header changes.

kevin: FYI — must coordinate with billing: if we throttle, we don't want to charge for rejected tokens. Mark: traceback in usage pipeline so cost = successful tokens only.

simon: On memory: use sharded ordinal map + LRU for per-key short buckets. Add metrics for cardinality of the short-bucket map so we can tune TTL.

erin: UX copy for Console: "Short burst allowance: Short-term request buffer that smooths brief spikes. Auto-managed by Redwood. Increase only for dedicated capacity." Keep it simple.

maria: Good, next steps: ashok prototype, kevin dashboard wire, erin UX copy + flag flow, sim tests in staging. I'll open matching tickets and link in this thread. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: Ticket created: PROXY-1227, DASH-334, UX-89, SIM-501.

kevin: Thanks — can we reconvene after sim data? 1792103900
